goal: Bound the rubric judge invocation with the default wall-clock deadline so a judge stream that never terminates is cancelled and surfaces a judge-infra timeout outcome under the default config, rather than stalling VALIDATING forever.

relevant: packages/flywheel-core/src/flywheel_core/grader_rubric.py -- around line 377 the `async for msg in _sdk_query(...)` judge stream is unbounded and sits outside the harness watchdog
packages/flywheel-core/src/flywheel_core/harness.py -- the _validate -> run_rubric_graders path does not wrap the judge in the working-agent watchdog
packages/flywheel-core/tests/test_grader_rubric.py -- keep this suite green; mirror its judge-invoke substitution for the new test
references: .flywheel/specs/00066-FEATURE-universal-deadlines.md -- criterion #3, the RubricJudgeError judge-infra failure path described in harness.py docstring (~line 3417)
constraints: Use the deadline primitive and resolved-config rubric ceiling from the prerequisite tasks.
Under default config the judge stream runs under a finite ceiling; a never-ending judge async-for must be cancelled.
A timeout surfaces as a judge-infra timeout outcome (the existing RubricJudgeError / judge-infra classification), distinguishable from a normal verdict.
Do not require the SDK extra at module top -- the judge path already lazy-imports via flywheel_core._sdk; keep it that way.
Add the pytest target so `uv run pytest -k rubric_judge_deadline` selects it.
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not modify or weaken assertions in test_grader_rubric.py.
Do not touch the working-agent, command-grader, docker, or autopilot paths here.
Do not make the rubric grader the authoritative grade -- this only bounds its invocation.
edge_cases: A judge whose `async for` never ends is cancelled in bounded wall time under DEFAULT config -- a streaming judge must not slip a silence timer.
A normally-returning judge still produces its verdict (no false-positive timeout).
